'''Webhelp''' was a [[human search engine]] and multi-national [[business process outsourcing]] company founded in Toronto, Canada, in 1999.
In 2023, [[Concentrix]] bought Webhelp.<ref name=":1" />

==History==

=== Founding and early years ===
Webhelp was founded in 1999 in Toronto, Canada, by Kerry Adler and Laura Hantho.<ref name=":2">{{Cite magazine |last=Pearson |first=Kali |date=September 2002 |title=The Answer Man |magazine=[[Profit (magazine)|Profit]] |volume=21 |issue=5 |issn=1183-1324}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hamilton |first=Tyler |date=1999-12-01 |title=Small Toronto firm gives Net searches a human touch |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-globe-and-mail-small-toronto-firm-gi/187465162/ |access-date=2025-12-26 |work=The Globe and Mail |pages=31 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Initially launched as Webhelp.com Inc., the company was a Delaware-registered corporation headquartered in Toronto. The company was established with a vision to revolutionize customer service through [[Human search engine|human-assisted online search]] and customer service technology.

The early business model of Webhelp centered on providing real-time, human-assisted customer support via online chat,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tomaiuolo |first=Nicholas G. |date=May 2000 |title=Aska and You May Receive: Commercial Reference Services on the Web |journal=Searcher |volume=8 |issue=5 |issn=1070-4795}}</ref> making it one of the pioneering ventures in outsourced customer experience solutions. The company's proprietary ARENA software solution was pivotal in its operations, facilitating back-office processing and online assistance. Webhelp soon secured major clients including [[Microsoft]], [[AOL]], and [[Sony]].<ref name=":2" />

=== Expansion to France and franchise agreement ===
In 2000, Webhelp expanded its operations into France under a franchise agreement with two French entrepreneurs, [[Olivier Duha]] and [[Frédéric Jousset]]. This significant expansion was formalized through the Technology and Trademark Agreement, signed on June 6, 2000, between Webhelp.com Inc. (Toronto) and the newly created Webhelp S.A. (France). The agreement granted Webhelp France a license to operate under the Webhelp brand and utilize its proprietary technology.

The franchise agreement outlined several critical stipulations:

* Webhelp.com Inc. remained the primary owner of the Webhelp trademark and technology.
* Webhelp S.A. paid an initial franchise fee of $1.5 million and royalties on revenue.
* Webhelp.com Inc. retained final approval on all technology changes and branding use.

Webhelp France was thus launched as a separate entity under license from the original Canadian company.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

=== Growth and evolution ===
Under Adler's leadership, Webhelp experienced rapid growth in North America, pioneering outsourced customer experience solutions. By 2002, Webhelp was recognized as one of Canada's fastest-growing startups, with a two-year revenue growth of 20,974%.<ref name=":2" />

Webhelp's expansion was not limited to North America. The company extended its operations to India, Sri Lanka, Mexico, and Budapest, providing global [[business process outsourcing]] (BPO) services. By 2003, Webhelp.com had transitioned from a consumer-facing search service to a corporate BPO provider, handling customer support and technical services for numerous Fortune 500 companies.

=== Separation of Webhelp France and later acquisitions ===
As Webhelp France continued to expand, it began operating more independently from Webhelp.com Inc. By 2005, Webhelp.com Inc. divested its remaining interest in Webhelp France, allowing the latter to function as a separate company. This separation marked a significant shift in the company's operational dynamics. Over the years, Webhelp France, under the leadership of Duha and Jousset, acquired additional outsourcing firms and eventually rebranded as the Webhelp Group.

In 2011, [[Charterhouse Capital Partners]] acquired a majority stake in Webhelp France, catalyzing its expansion across Europe. Further solidifying its market position, in 2019, [[Groupe Bruxelles Lambert]] (GBL) purchased a controlling interest in the company. This acquisition was followed by a merger in 2023, when [[Concentrix]] acquired Webhelp.<ref name=":1" />

In February 2013, the group purchased [[Falkirk]] call centre firm HEROtsc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-business-21508899|title=Falkirk call centre firm HEROtsc sold to Webhelp Group|last=|first=|date=19 February 2013|website=BBC News|publisher=|access-date=16 November 2016}}</ref> In 2014, Webhelp UK became a shirt sponsor of [[Falkirk F.C.]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Butcher |first1=Lucy |title=Falkirk FC name new sponsor |url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/falkirk_fc_name_new_sponsor/ |website=SportsPro |access-date=13 January 2023 |date=14 March 2014}}</ref>

In 2013, Webhelp was awarded a £1.5 million Regional Selective Assistance grant from [[Scottish Development International]], helping to create 400 new jobs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Salmond welcomes 400 new jobs in central belt |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/13103777.salmond-welcomes-400-new-jobs-central-belt/ |website=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]] |date=8 May 2013 |access-date=13 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, it planned to move 120 jobs handling calls for [[Thomas Cook]] from Falkirk to South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Swindon |first1=Peter |title=Call centre firm fielding Thomas Cook calls sends jobs to South Africa despite £500k grant from Scottish Enterprise |url=https://www.sundaypost.com/fp/call-centre-firm-fielding-thomas-cook-calls-sends-jobs-to-south-africa-despite-500k-grant-from-scottish-enterprise/ |website=The Sunday Post |date=20 January 2019 |access-date=13 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Call centre firm Webhelp to cut 120 staff as jobs go to Africa |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/call-centre-firm-webhelp-to-cut-120-staff-as-jobs-go-to-africa-hsx65wsll |website=The Times |date=21 January 2019 |access-date=13 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2015, Webhelp took over from [[Serco]] the running of two call centres in [[Aintree]] and [[Bolton]] serving the [[The Very Group|Shop Direct Group]].<ref name=":0" /> Several months later, it proposed moving most of the operation to South Africa.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Butler |first1=Sarah |title=Webhelp call centres for Shop Direct to close with 700 jobs lost |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2015/dec/03/webhelp-call-centres-for-shop-direct-to-close-with-700-jobs-lost |access-date=13 January 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=3 December 2015 |language=en}}</ref>

In June 2016, Webhelp acquired GoExcellent, a Scandinavian customer experience firm which operates nine centers across Sweden, Finland, Norway and Denmark, and employs 1,700 people. This acquisition allowed for the launch of Webhelp Nordic, and increased Webhelp's projected 2016 turnover to an estimated $1 billion (725 million Euros).<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-eco/2016/06/23/97002-20160623FILWWW00089-webhelp-rachete-le-groupe-goexcellent.php|title=Webhelp rachète le groupe GoExcellent|last=lefigaro.fr|newspaper=Le Figaro|access-date=2016-11-07}}</ref>

By November 2020, Webhelp employed more than 55,000 people in over 35 countries.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Stewart |title=Frédéric Jousset: the Louvre donor building a superyacht to show art around the world |url=https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/luxury/article/frederic-jousset-the-louvre-donor-building-a-superyacht-to-show-art-around-the-world-hbdrxfljl |website=The Times |access-date=13 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

On 29 March 2023, Concentrix agreed to buy Webhelp in a $4.8 billion deal.<ref name=":1">{{cite news |title=Concentrix looks beyond North America with $4.8 bln deal for Webhelp |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/concentrix-acquire-webhelp-48-bln-deal-2023-03-29/ |access-date=1 June 2023 |work=Reuters |agency=Reuters |date=29 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In September 2023, it was announced the [[European Commission]] had approved the acquisition, under EU Merger Regulations.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 15, 2023 |title=Mergers: Commission authorizes acquisition of Webhelp by Concentrix |work=EU Reporter |url=https://www.eureporter.co/politics/european-commission/2023/09/15/mergers-commission-authorizes-acquisition-of-webhelp-by-concentrix/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Charlie |date=2023-09-29 |title=Concentrix to Rebrand After Wrapping Up Its $4BN Webhelp Deal |url=https://www.cxtoday.com/voice-of-the-customer/concentrix-to-rebrand-after-wrapping-up-its-4bn-webhelp-deal/ |access-date=2024-12-04 |website=CX Today |language=en-GB}}</ref>
